key_insight: A deep learning surrogate can directly predict full-field microstructure response, enabling fast optimization of polycrystalline copper for competing spall and yield strength targets.
engineering_relevance: The framework makes expensive CPFE-based microstructure design practical by preserving the spatial and temporal detail needed for performance assessment while cutting optimization cost by orders of magnitude.
method: 3D U-Net maps 3D polycrystalline microstructures to velocity histories from plate-impact simulations.
Stochastic microstructure generation plus derivative-free optimization searches the design space.
DCRR using MMD monitors distribution shift to flag surrogate reliability during optimization.
evidence_signal: Validated optimal designs matched CPFE results with less than 3% prediction error, and surrogate-driven optimization reduced cumulative evaluation time by about four orders of magnitude.
watch_item: Reliability depends on staying near the training-data distribution, so extrapolation beyond the DCRR region may weaken surrogate accuracy.
paper_title: Deep learning driven framework for optimization of polycrystalline microstructures under competing strength requirements
